post.description: Creates the person, their first Project and its API key in one call, and signs them in. This is US0: the API key exists at the moment of registration and not after it. The key is shown here and nowhere else — only its prefix and a hash are stored, so no endpoint can return it again. An email with a verification link goes to the address: the `test` key works without it, a `live` key waits for it.

post.description: The other half of the webhooks, and it does not replace the per-Request `callbackUrl` — ADR-0014 decided the two stand beside each other. A Request that carries a `callbackUrl` **and** matches a subscription here produces two deliveries of the same event, to the two addresses; delivery is at-least-once by PRD §4.1 and both carry the same `id` and the same `responseId`, so a receiver behind both deduplicates them exactly as it deduplicates a retry. Every delivery is signed with the Project’s `webhookSigningSecret` — the same one that signs a per-Request callback, because there is only one. The URL is checked before the row exists: `https` only, no credentials in the userinfo, and every address the hostname resolves to must be public.

post.description: Names the Requests this Device currently has on screen and holds until one of them stops being pending — answered from another phone, dismissed, expired, or withdrawn by the agent. Always a `200`; an empty `settled` means the window closed with every card still true, and the app re-issues with whatever it is still showing. `wait: 0` does not wait at all, which is the reconciliation an app performs on returning to the foreground. Ids that are not yours, and ids that never existed, are simply not reported on. A Request past its own `expiresAt` is reported once the sweep has closed it, at most a minute later; until then the app already draws it as finished from the `expiresAt` every row carries.

200.description: The named Requests that have stopped asking — empty if none had.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

The Surface goes out exactly as the agent sent it; the server neither renders nor inspects it (ADR-0003). Works for a Message in either list.

delete.description: The person emptying their own mailbox (PRD §8). What is destroyed is the **Content** — the Surface, the notification block, the quick actions and, on a Request that was answered, the `context` of the Response. What survives is the row and its Metadata, so `GET /v1/requests/{id}` still tells the agent that this Request was asked and how it ended, with nothing left in it to read, and the product’s own count of completed HITL loops reports the same number as before (ADR-0003). Irreversible, and there is no undo. A Request still `pending` is **dismissed** first — the agent receives `message.dismissed` and an `await` on it resolves rather than hanging on something nobody can answer any more. After this the Message is in neither list and opens from nowhere, so a second `DELETE` answers `404`.

post.description: The Device confirming the push reached this phone, which is the only thing that actually knows: FCM confirms it *queued* a notification, not that it landed. Idempotent, and the first Device wins — a Message fans out to every Device of the recipient (PRD §4.3), and the receipt means *first confirmed*, not *all confirmed*. Called from the background handler when a push wakes a dead app, so it is expected to run without anything being opened. It never changes a `status`.

post.description: Records that the person saw it. Idempotent: the first read wins and a repeat returns the same `readAt`. Stamps `deliveredAt` too when nothing had — a Message can only be read on a phone it reached — so an `informational` Message travels `delivered → read` even when the push never arrived and the person found it in the list (PRD §4.2). For such a Message this is what moves it to the History: it has no `pending` and no expiry, so being read is how it finishes. It never changes a `status`: a Request is still answered or dismissed through `POST /v1/requests/{id}/response` or `/dismiss`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `messageId` of the row on screen.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

get.summary: Every Project this person owns, with its API keys

post.description: A Project is born the way PRD §4.4 describes one: two environments, a `test` API key returned in full and never again, the owner as its default recipient, an empty inbox. The key comes back beside the Project rather than inside it, because it is the one thing in this answer that exists in a readable form exactly once — copy it now. Nothing about the first Project changes: registration still creates one, so a person who wants exactly one never comes here.

201.description: The Project, and the `test` key it was born with.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_revoked`.

402.description: `plan_limit_reached`. The account already holds as many Projects as its plan allows; deleted Projects are not counted. The message names the plan, its limit and where to upgrade. An account above the limit — after moving to a smaller plan — keeps every Project it has, and creates none until it is back under.

post.summary: Create a Project, and read its first key once

patch.description: The two editable things about a Project, and either may be sent alone. `name` is what registration calls `Default`, because US0 hands out a Project so that a key has somewhere to belong — this is where a person names it once they know what it is for. `retentionDays` is how long the **Content** of this Project’s Messages is kept: after that many days from when a Message was sent, its Surface, notification block, quick actions and any Response `context` are destroyed, while the row and its Metadata stay, so the agent still sees that the Request was asked and how it ended (ADR-0003). `null` means never, and is the default — a mailbox that empties itself without anybody having asked loses messages. Shortening the window applies to what is already there, within the hour.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The `projectId` registration returned.

200.description: The Project as it now stands, keys included.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_revoked`.

404.description: `project_not_found`. The same answer for a Project that is somebody else’s and for one that never existed — telling them apart would make this endpoint a way of asking which ids are real.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. The name must be between 1 and 80 characters; `retentionDays` a whole number of days between 1 and 3650, or `null`.

patch.summary: Change a Project’s name or its retention window

delete.description: Its API keys are revoked, the **Content** of every Message it holds is destroyed — surface, quick actions, notification text and any Response `context`, exactly as deleting a Thread destroys it — and the Project stops being listed. What stays is the metadata: the rows, their status and their dates, so the loops a person completed here still count as having happened (ADR-0016). Any Request still `pending` is settled as `dismissed` first, so an agent waiting on one is told rather than left holding. **The last Project cannot be deleted**: registration promises everybody one, and an account with none would have no way back.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The Project to delete.

404.description: `project_not_found`. Somebody else’s, never existed, or already deleted — the same answer for all three.

post.description: The second and last place a whole credential exists in a readable form — the first is registration. Only its prefix and a SHA-256 are stored, so nothing can return it again. `environment` says which half of the Project the key speaks for and is required: the prefix it comes back with — `sk_test_…` or `sk_live_…` — is what an SDK reads its own environment from, and a key of one half neither creates nor reads the Requests of the other. Minting does not revoke anything: rotating is mint, put the new key in the agent, then revoke the old one, in that order, so that nothing stops working in between. A `live` key needs the account’s email verified; a `test` key never does, and the `live` keys minted before stay valid either way.

The row is never deleted: the Messages it sent point at it, and that is what answers "what did this key send" without an audit log. Repeatable — revoking a revoked key changes nothing and keeps the original date.

They belong to the User, so they hold across every Project they own, and they survive a reinstall: the phone reads them back from here rather than remembering them locally.

An agent holding one of those keys is refused with `401` from then on, a long poll waiting on one of those Requests included, and callbacks still being retried are dropped. A receipt is emailed to the address the account had.

One-shot Requests are Threads of one and are listed too — their `threadKey` is null. The list is scoped to the half of the Project the key belongs to: a `sk_test_…` never sees a live conversation.

A one-shot Thread has no key and is not reachable here — read its Request with `GET /v1/requests/{id}`.

With `wait` the call holds until something arrives **in this Thread**: a notification, or a Message of any other conversation, never resolves it. Always a `200`; an empty `items` means the window closed with nothing new, and the app re-issues from the same `after`.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

404.description: `thread_not_found`. A Thread belonging to another person answers the same way as one that does not exist.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `after` must be a whole number; `limit` 1 to 100; `wait` a whole number of seconds between 0 and 30.

delete.description: Everything said in this Thread, thrown away at once (PRD §8). What is destroyed is the **Content** of every Message in it — the Surfaces, the notification blocks, the quick actions and the `context` of every Response — and what survives is the rows and their Metadata, so the agent still sees that the conversation happened and how each Request ended, with nothing left in it to read (ADR-0003). Requests still `pending` are **dismissed** first, one `message.dismissed` each, so nothing is left `await`ing on a question nobody can answer any more. The Thread itself is not removed and its ordinals are not reused: a Message sent to it afterwards continues the sequence. Irreversible, and there is no undo.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `threadId` carried by every row of the Inbox and of the History.

get.description: Twelve weeks of HITL loops completed — the North Star, read from the same SQL view that defines it and summed over the Projects you own — with the supporting metrics the data actually permits: time to your first message, Requests asked per week, response rate, median time to answer, the share of Requests that carried rich UI rather than only approve/reject, and the delivery rate. **Every number is about one half of your Projects**, `live` unless you ask for `test`: a rate that mixed the rehearsals into the real Requests would be a number about nothing. Each field says what it counts and over what window, because a number without a definition is worse than no number. **The last week of the series is always understated** — the Requests asked in it are still pending — so read the last complete one. Nothing here reads inside a `surface` or a Response `context`, and no metric is derived from one: this endpoint counts statuses, timestamps and whether a column is null.

200.description: The metrics. An account that has sent nothing answers with twelve weeks of zeros and every rate `null` — «nothing has concluded yet» rather than «nothing concluded».

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `environment` must be `test` or `live`.

get.summary: The North Star, and the metrics of PRD §9 beside it

get.description: Every Message sent from the Projects you own, newest first, filterable by Project, half, status, type and Thread. A row is **metadata and the notification title**: `interactionType`, priority, status, the delivery and read receipts, the deadline, and the action a Response carried — never the Surface the agent built, never the `context` an answer came with. Requests whose Content has been deleted are listed with `contentDeleted` and an empty title, because what was asked and how it ended survives what was written (ADR-0016). Paged with an opaque cursor: hand `nextCursor` back unchanged, and `null` means the end.

200.description: One page, and `total`: how many rows the filters match in all. An account that has sent nothing, and a filter that matches nothing, both answer with an empty list, no cursor and a total of zero.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_revoked`.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `limit` between 1 and 100, `environment` `test` or `live`, `status` one of the five, `type` `request` or `notification`, and `cursor` a `nextCursor` this endpoint returned. A `projectId` or a `threadId` that is not yours is not an error: it narrows the list to nothing, for the reason every read over this table answers the same about a Project that is somebody else’s and one that never existed.

get.summary: What your agents sent, newest first

get.description: The row of the list, and beside it what a trail needs: the key that sent it, the Devices that received it, read it and answered it, the `Idempotency-Key` the agent chose, whether it asked for a `callbackUrl` of its own, and the Project’s standing subscriptions in that half. Still metadata: never the Surface, never the `context` an answer came with, and never the `callbackUrl` itself — a workflow engine’s resume URL is a credential.

info.title: Nibify API
info.description: The channel on which AI agents push interactive UI to a person and receive an answer back. This document is the source of truth every client is generated from.

code.description: What went wrong, for a program to branch on.
x-enum-descriptions: The request could not be read: the body is not valid JSON, or is cut short.
The password reset token has already been used, or has expired.
The email verification link has expired, or was never issued. Ask for another.
The login token in the QR has already been used, or has expired. Scan the QR the dashboard shows now.
The credential is missing, malformed or unknown. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
The API key was revoked. Create a new one in the dashboard.
The session was signed out. Sign in again.
The session belongs to a browser, and only the app may call this endpoint.
The email and password do not match an account.

The account’s plan allows no more of this: its live Messages for the month, or its Projects. Nothing was created. Not worth retrying until the month turns or the plan changes; the `test` Environment is never counted.
The password given to confirm this act is not the account’s. Nothing was changed.
Registration is by invitation, and this email is not on the list. Nothing was created.
A live API key needs the account’s email verified first. Follow the link in the email, or ask for another.
The endpoint only accepts submissions from the Nibify site.
The submission looked automated and was not recorded.
No endpoint answers this method and path, or a value in the path cannot name anything.
No Request with that id is visible to this credential.
No Message with that id is visible to this credential.
No Thread with that id or key is visible to this credential.
No Project of yours has that id.
The Project has no API key with that id.
No Device of yours has that id.
The Project has no webhook endpoint with that id.
An account already exists for this email. Sign in instead.
The account’s email is already verified. Nothing was sent.
The account’s only Project cannot be deleted. Create another first.
Every test key of the Project is revoked, and a demo is sent under one. Create a test key first.
This Environment of the Project already subscribes that URL.
The Request was already answered, and the answer can be read.
The Request expired before it was answered.
The person already dismissed the Request.
The agent already cancelled the Request.
The body is larger than the API accepts.
The body is not `application/json`.
The body or the query string does not match the expected shape. `details` points at each field.
The Idempotency-Key was already used for a different body. Use a new key, or resend the original body unchanged.
`callbackUrl` cannot be called: only public `https` endpoints are.
The surface does not conform to the catalog, or does not fit the endpoint. `details` names the component and property.
The webhook URL cannot be called: only public `https` endpoints are.
A limit is spent: the Project’s per-second or daily one in this Environment, or the attempts at an authentication endpoint. Retry after the seconds in `Retry-After`.
Any other request the API could not accept. The status says which.
Something failed on Nibify’s side. Retrying may succeed.

message.description: What went wrong, in a sentence for a person reading a log.

details.description: One entry for each problem found in what you sent, when the error can point at it.

pointer.description: Where the problem is, as a dotted path into what you sent: `notification.title`.

component.description: The `id` of the Surface component at fault, when the problem is inside a Surface.

property.description: The property of that component at fault, when there is one.

token.description: The `token` parameter in the fragment of the URL the QR encodes.

url.description: What the QR encodes: an `https` URL with the token in its fragment, `#token=…`. The app reads the fragment, and a server this URL is ever opened against never receives it.

expiresAt.description: Ten minutes after it was minted. Ask for another one then.

name.description: The name the person sees, free text.

icon.description: An icon for the sender, free text, kept and returned as sent. Nothing draws it: the person sees the sender by its `name`.

sender.description: Who the person sees the Request as coming from.

title.description: The title of the push and of its Inbox row.

body.description: The text of the push and of its Inbox row.

quickActions.description: Buttons on the push itself, answerable from the lock screen.

name.description: The action the button dispatches, and the `actionName` of the Response it produces. With a `surface`, it must be an action the Surface dispatches.

label.description: The button’s text on the notification.

notification.description: What the push says, and the buttons it offers.

surface.description: The interactive UI the person answers in, checked against the catalog. Without it, the push and its `quickActions` are the whole Request.

root.description: The `id` of the component the Surface is drawn from: always `root`, and one of `components` must carry it.

dataModel.description: The flat JSON state the components bind to by JSON Pointer, and the source of the values an action sends back.

components.description: The components, as a flat list, each one checked against the catalog.

expiresAt.description: When the Request expires if nobody has answered it, in the future. Without it, the Request waits indefinitely.

callbackUrl.description: A public `https` URL called once, with a signed `POST`, when the Request reaches a terminal state.

requestId.description: The Request’s id: read it, wait for it, withdraw it or nudge it by this.

sequence.description: The Request’s position in its Thread, starting at 1.

interactionType.description: Inferred, never sent: `conversation` when the Request joined a Thread that already had Messages, `action` otherwise.

status.description: The status the Request has now. On an idempotent replay, whatever the original has become since.

expiresAt.description: When the Request expires, or null if it never does.

environment.description: The Environment of the API key that created it.

minCatalogVersion.description: The lowest catalog version that can draw the Surface, worked out by the server. Null when there is no Surface.

code.description: What the warning is about, for a program to branch on.

message.description: The same warning, in a sentence for a person.

warnings.description: What did not stop the Message but changes how it is shown: `catalog_version_too_low` when no installed app can draw the Surface.

status.description: Where the Request is: `pending` until it reaches one of the four terminal states.

sourceComponentId.description: The `id` of the component the person answered with, or `notification` for a quick action on the push.

context.description: The values the action sent back, or null when it sent none or the person has since deleted the content.

clientTimestamp.description: When the person answered, by the phone’s clock.

response.description: The person’s answer: present exactly when `status` is `answered`.
